issues.body: `attested_review_head` iterates records newest-first but skips every record whose cause is not `human-arm`, then returns an older `human-arm` head. This contradicts the function's own `Newest receipt wins` invariant. For example, authenticated bot history `[human-arm(head=live), injection(head=live)]` returns the old human-arm head and `approval_coverage` admits `covers-head`, even though the newest park episode asserts an injection stop rather than a completed approval awaiting arm. The existing off-cause test contains only the off-cause receipt, so it does not exercise this supersession seam. Historical review evidence must not be resurrected across a newer park episode.
issues.fix_hint: Select the newest authenticated well-formed park-reason record first; attest a head only if that newest record has `cause=human-arm`, otherwise return no attestation/refuse. Add a literal end-to-end case with an older matching human-arm receipt followed by a newer authenticated off-cause receipt, and assert that it cannot produce `covers-head` or exit 0.
issues.title: A later off-cause park does not supersede an older human-arm attestation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-2 author-forgery fix remains intact, but the new receipt selector does not implement its stated newest-receipt authority rule. It selects the newest `human-arm` receipt while silently stepping past any later authenticated park-reason receipt for another cause. That can resurrect a superseded approval binding from an older park episode and report `covers-head`, so this round introduces a new major trust-plane finding and is regressing relative to round 2's clean approval.
